Polywrap Films is our only qualified supplier of the 23-micron stretch film used on all four pallet wrappers. Qualifying a new supplier takes about four months (trials plus customer sign-off). We use roughly 9 tonnes a month.

state: Incident note, Saturday 24 Oct, 11:30. Brightloom's autumn code FALL15 was meant to give 15% off orders over £60 on full-price home textiles. It went live at 08:00 on the site banner and in an email to 48,000 subscribers. A setup error left out the £60 minimum and let the code stack with the existing 20% clearance discount, so clearance items are going out at 35% off. Since 08:00, 1,140 orders have used FALL15; a normal Saturday morning brings about 400 orders in total. A deal-forum thread titled "Brightloom stacking glitch", posted at 09:50, has 600 replies. On clearance items at 35% off our margin is about -4%; on full-price items at 15% off it is about +28%. 62% of FALL15 orders contain clearance items. Our terms let us cancel orders placed at an obvious pricing error, but 410 FALL15 orders have already been dispatched. Correcting the code's rules takes about 10 minutes in the admin panel; the email cannot be recalled.

Applicant: Fernhill Men's Shed, a volunteer-run group founded in 2019 with 46 members, mostly retired men. It meets three days a week in a borrowed garage. Request: 4,000, made up of a dust extraction unit (1,650), a bandsaw (1,100) and first-aid and machine-safety training for 12 volunteers (1,250). Two supplier quotes are attached for each tool, and the cheaper quote was chosen each time. The group holds 2,300 of its own money.

Letters of support come from the local GP practice, which says it has referred 'a number of patients' to the shed for loneliness, and from the parish council. The garage owner has given the group notice to leave by 31 March 2027. The group says it is 'in talks' about a unit on the industrial estate but has no agreement yet; the tools would move with them. The group's last grant from the Chest (2024, 1,500 for hand tools) was spent and reported on time.

Scoring guidance: deliverability means whether the group can carry out the project as planned within the next 12 months. Grants may be made conditional on a named event before payment.

Scam claim note, 2 December 2026.

Customer Peter Lund, 58, made two transfers from his current account to an account named 'J. Morgan Logistics': 1,500 on 24 November and 3,200 on 26 November. They were a deposit and the balance for a used campervan advertised on a well-known classifieds website at 4,700. Peter's own notes say this was about half the usual price for that model and year. He never saw the van; the seller said it was in storage abroad and would be delivered after payment.

On the first payment, our name check showed 'close match' and no scam warning was shown. On the second payment, the name check showed 'no match' and the app showed the warning: 'Could this be a scam? Do not pay for goods you have not seen.' Peter ticked 'I understand' and continued.

Policy: customers are reimbursed for scam losses unless they were grossly negligent. Going ahead despite a specific, relevant warning and a 'no match' result counts towards gross negligence for that payment. Vulnerability must be considered. Peter has no recorded vulnerabilities. The receiving bank froze 600 left in the account on 28 November.

criteria.close match: The name was close to the account name

criteria.refund first only: Reimburse the 1,500 payment but not the 3,200 payment

some signs: One or two odd details that could easily be explained

Version 5.3 adds the new budgeting screen, which marketing has announced for 2 Nov with a press briefing that morning. The 5.3 build went to app store review on 22 Oct; review normally takes 1 to 3 days, but twice this year it took 6 days. Beta: 420 testers, crash-free sessions 99.1% against a target of at least 99.5%. Nearly all crashes come from one Android phone model, used by about 4% of our users, and happen when the budgeting screen is opened; the rest of the app works on that model. Our rollout tool can release to 1%, 10%, 50% or 100% of users and can block specific device models from receiving an update. From 14:02 to 15:47 on 22 Oct, a caching bug made some users see other companies' project names in the 'recent projects' menu. Logs show 312 such views, involving project names from 41 customer companies. Only project names were shown: no files, comments, task details or member lists. state: Incident prep note, 22 Nov 2027, 09:30. On 20 Nov at 16:05 an outside researcher emailed security@ to report that our document app's public share links (/s/{token}) still return a file when the last 4 characters of the token are removed, because the lookup uses a prefix match. The researcher attached two sample links that opened other customers' files: a payroll spreadsheet with staff names and salaries, and a signed contract. The email sat unread in the shared inbox over the weekend; the on-call engineer read it at 09:12 today and reproduced the flaw by 09:25. Code history shows the prefix match shipped in release 3.14 on 2 Oct. Access logs since 2 Oct show 1,840 successful requests using shortened tokens, from 23 distinct IP addresses, 2 of which belong to the researcher. A patch that requires an exact token match is written and tested; deploying it takes 15 minutes. Security policy: confirmed exposure of customer personal data is reported to the privacy officer within 24 hours of confirmation, and affected customers are told within 72 hours of confirmation.

q1.instructions: The researcher's report included examples of exposed files.

criteria.true: Sample links to other customers' files were attached.
criteria.false: The report described the flaw without examples.

q2.instructions: The logs suggest that people other than the researcher used the flaw.

criteria.true: Shortened-token requests came from addresses not linked to the researcher.
criteria.false: All such requests came from the researcher.

q3.instructions: Judged by what stops further exposure soonest, what should the on-call engineer do first?

criteria.Reply to researcher: Thank the researcher and agree disclosure terms.

q4.instructions: How severe is this incident?
criteria: Informational: No real weakness.
Low: A weakness with no realistic path to customer data.
Medium: Customer data could be reached, but no sign it has been.
High: Customer data reached by a known party, flaw now closed.
Critical: Customer personal data reached by unknown parties while the flaw is still open.

q5.instructions: Which customers should be treated as affected and told?

criteria.Two sample owners: Only the owners of the two files in the report.
criteria.All customers: Every customer of the document app.
criteria.No one yet: Nobody until a full external audit is complete.
criteria.Owners of accessed files: Owners of every file fetched with a shortened token since 2 Oct.

state: Duty scientist's note, 07:30, 18 July 2027. Routine overnight samples from Hillcrest service reservoir: total coliforms detected in 2 of 3 samples (target: none detected); E. coli not detected in any sample; chlorine residual 0.08 mg/L (operating minimum 0.2 mg/L). Hillcrest supplies about 6,400 homes and St Anne's Hospital. Yesterday at 15:00 a roof hatch on the reservoir was found unlatched after storm damage; it was secured at 16:10. Customer contacts since midnight: 3 about taste, none about illness. Water safety procedure: (1) if E. coli is found in any sample, issue a boil-water notice at once. (2) If coliforms are found while chlorine is below the operating minimum: raise chlorine dosing; isolate the reservoir if an alternative supply exists; resample within 6 hours; inform the health authority the same day. A boil-water notice then follows only if resampling finds E. coli or the health authority advises one. The procedure says nothing about contacting individual customers. Westfield reservoir can supply Hillcrest's zone for up to 48 hours.

Night shift report, Freezer Room 2, Delmar Cold Storage, 14 January 2027, written by shift lead P. Oyelaran.

At 02:10 the room temperature alarm sounded with the display at -12 C. The room set point is -20 C. Standard client contracts require product to be kept at or below -18 C, and any period above -15 C lasting more than 2 hours must be reported to the client within 24 hours. The on-call technician arrived at 03:05, found that the evaporator fan motor had failed, and had a new motor running by 04:20. Hourly readings: 02:10 -12 C, 03:00 -10 C, 04:00 -9 C, 05:00 -13 C, 06:00 -16 C, 07:00 -19 C. Doors stayed shut and no stock was moved during the event.

The room holds stock for three clients: Polar Peas (220 pallets of frozen vegetables), Nordic Bakery (80 pallets of par-baked bread) and Frostline Ice Cream (45 pallets). Frostline's contract has an extra clause: if any reading in the room is above -15 C, all Frostline pallets go on QA hold until Frostline's own quality team inspects them. Under all contracts, the decision to release or dispose of a client's goods belongs to the client, not to Delmar.

Hana runs a shop selling hand-dyed yarn on an online marketplace. The marketplace measures sellers over the last 90 days: the late shipment rate (late orders divided by all orders) must stay below 4%, and the order defect rate (orders with a buyer claim, a one- or two-star review, or a refund, divided by all orders) must stay below 1%.
